title: The Secret Science of Glowing Animals

media.title: File:South Fork Clackamas Wild and Scenic River (28287613250).webm

script: Why do some living things glow in the dark? It is all thanks to a chemical reaction inside their bodies. Creatures like fireflies, deep-sea jellyfish, and glowing fungi mix a light-emitting molecule called luciferin with an enzyme named luciferase. When oxygen is added, energy is released not as heat, but as vibrant visible light. In the pitch-black ocean, animals use this natural superpower called bioluminescence to hide from hungry predators, attract potential mates, or lure unsuspecting prey. It is one of nature's most brilliant survival tricks, proving that sometimes, making your own light is the ultimate evolutionary advantage.
